headlines.finding: Support calls score lowest (2.933) and external highest (3.95); support minus external is -1.017 (95% CI [-1.433, -0.588], p=0.0002), and still -0.747 (CI [-1.193, -0.304]) under the title-rule labels. In support calls customers carry the negativity: 35.4% of customer turns vs 2.1% of staff turns are negative (gap 0.334, CI [0.236, 0.429], customer more negative in 22 of 30 calls).
headlines.so_what: Support leader: track the customer-side score, not the call average, and compare each type only to its own baseline.
headlines.could_be_wrong_if: Support calls are selected for trouble, so the gap shows what the call is for rather than how well it was handled. Support vs internal and external vs internal are fragile (see q1_pairwise_title_rule).

headlines.finding: March dip of -0.884 (CI [-1.238, -0.515]) is concentrated in outage-touching calls (within March 2.565 vs 3.615, n=[23, 13]). Excluding calls that touch the outage the dip is -0.318 (CI [-0.81, 0.157], n March 13): not distinguishable from zero. Call-type mix does not explain it (type-adjusted monthly means {'2026-02': 3.728, '2026-03': 2.974, '2026-04': 3.853}). External April vs pre-outage: -0.161 (CI [-0.6, 0.263]).
headlines.so_what: Engineering lead and support lead: the outage, not a general slide, explains most of the dip, and external calls were back near pre-outage levels by April.
headlines.could_be_wrong_if: The outage flag is an LLM judgment, partly definitional; in the candidate's 20-call check it missed 3 and never over-flagged, so 42 is probably a floor (42 calls): a call about an outage is tense. Only 13 March calls remain after exclusion, so a residual dip cannot be ruled out.

headlines.finding: The outage shows up in all three call types: 42 calls touch it ({'support': 10, 'external': 18, 'internal': 14}), peaking in the week of Mar 9 and continuing into April. External calls: pre-outage 4.367 (n=15), acute Mar 10-31 2.625 (n=8), April 4.206 (n=17). Of 9 accounts with an outage-touching support call and an external call, customer scores ended lower than they started for 4 (including summittrust, stratoscloud, clearwatermed, ridgelinelogistics) and higher for 3 (trailheadmkt, cobaltsoftware, forgeindustries).
headlines.so_what: Sales manager: put the accounts that ended lower, and those with no call after mid-March (northstarpharma, ridgelinelogistics), on a follow-up list.
headlines.could_be_wrong_if: Account comparisons are 2-4 calls with different purposes (renewal vs support), so they are leads to check, not conclusions. Dates in the dataset are inconsistent about when the outage started.

headlines.finding: 78 of 100 calls end warmer than they start, 21 are flat and 1 gets worse; the mean uplift is 0.5 (support), 0.55 (external), 0.45 (internal). 16 calls still end at 2.5 or below ({'support': 10, 'external': 4, 'internal': 2}).
headlines.so_what: Support leader: the useful signal is the list of calls that end strained, not the average uplift.
headlines.could_be_wrong_if: The uplift is nearly uniform, which points to the scripted shape of the calls and the rubric's relief rule more than to customer satisfaction. In support, per-turn negativity barely falls (0.182 to 0.158) while the trajectory score rises.

headlines.finding: Our score tracks the provided score (r=0.963, mean absolute difference 0.234, ours higher by 0.094 on average, CI [0.041, 0.148]); no call differs by 1 or more (max 0.7). 8 calls differ by 0.6 or more, 5 of them internal outage calls where ours is higher (internal outage-touching offset 0.236 vs 0.071 elsewhere). Of 444 turns the provided labels call positive and we call neutral, 380 are staff turns.
headlines.so_what: Analytics owner: the provided score tracks the severity of the situation, ours tracks the tone; report both, and do not mix them in one trend.
headlines.could_be_wrong_if: There are no gold labels. Agreement with an upstream AI output is consistency, not accuracy, and ours is also an LLM judgment with the D8 design choices (courtesy is neutral, lower tie-break).
